tasks.name: Handle blocking work, cancellation, and async resources

concepts.name: asyncio.run entry point
concepts.description: asyncio.run(coro) creates and manages an event loop for a top-level coroutine and closes it when the coroutine completes.

concepts.name: asyncio.gather
concepts.description: asyncio.gather(*aws) runs awaitables concurrently and returns successful results in the same order as the supplied awaitables.

concepts.name: asyncio.TaskGroup
concepts.description: asyncio.TaskGroup is an async context manager for structured concurrency: created tasks are awaited when the context exits and failures are handled as a group.

concepts.name: asyncio.Semaphore
concepts.description: asyncio.Semaphore limits how many tasks may enter a protected section concurrently by maintaining an async counter.

concepts.name: asyncio.Queue backpressure
concepts.description: asyncio.Queue coordinates producers and consumers without blocking the event loop; a positive maxsize makes put() wait when the queue is full.

concepts.name: asyncio.Lock
concepts.description: asyncio.Lock serializes access to a shared async resource so only one task holds the critical section at a time.

concepts.name: asyncio.to_thread
concepts.description: asyncio.to_thread(func, *args) runs a synchronous callable in a worker thread and returns an awaitable for its result.

concepts.name: asyncio.timeout
concepts.description: asyncio.timeout(delay) is an async context manager that limits the time spent awaiting operations inside its block.

concepts.name: Cancellation cleanup
concepts.description: Cancelling an asyncio task injects CancelledError at an await point; cleanup should generally happen in finally and cancellation should normally propagate.

concepts.name: async for
concepts.description: async for consumes an asynchronous iterator by awaiting its __anext__ method between iterations.

concepts.name: AnyIO task groups
concepts.description: AnyIO provides structured-concurrency APIs that can run on supported async backends; create_task_group() scopes sibling tasks.

concepts.name: HTTPX AsyncClient
concepts.description: HTTPX AsyncClient is an async HTTP client; requests are awaited and the client is typically reused inside an async context manager.

questions.prompt: Use structured concurrency for the child tasks.

content.template:
async def process_all(items):
    async with {{answer}} as tg:
        for item in items:
            tg.create_task(process(item))

questions.explanation: asyncio.TaskGroup is an async context manager for structured concurrency: created tasks are awaited when the context exits and failures are handled as a group. async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: tg.create_task(work()) keeps related child tasks scoped to the block. Do not swallow CancelledError inside TaskGroup children without a deliberate reason; structured-concurrency machinery relies on cancellation.

questions.prompt: Protect the shared-state update with the existing asyncio lock.

content.template:
lock = asyncio.Lock()

async def increment(key):
    {{answer}}
        counts[key] += 1

questions.explanation: asyncio.Lock serializes access to a shared async resource so only one task holds the critical section at a time. async with lock: state[key] += 1 automatically releases the lock even if the body raises. A lock protects a critical section; it does not make blocking synchronous work safe to run on the event loop.

questions.prompt: Apply one timeout to all awaits in the block.

content.template:
async def load():
    {{answer}}
        profile = await get_profile()
        permissions = await get_permissions()
    return profile, permissions

questions.explanation: asyncio.timeout(delay) is an async context manager that limits the time spent awaiting operations inside its block. async with asyncio.timeout(2): result = await fetch() scopes a timeout around one or more awaits. Timeout handling uses cancellation internally, so code that swallows CancelledError can interfere with structured async behavior.

questions.prompt: Ensure the lease is released even when the task is cancelled.
questions.explanation: Cancelling an asyncio task injects CancelledError at an await point; cleanup should generally happen in finally and cancellation should normally propagate. Use try/finally around resources that must be released when a task is cancelled. CancelledError directly subclasses BaseException, and swallowing it can break TaskGroup and timeout behavior.

questions.prompt: Create an AnyIO task group.

content.template:
import anyio

async def main(items):
    async with {{answer}} as tg:
        for item in items:
            tg.start_soon(worker, item)

questions.explanation: AnyIO provides structured-concurrency APIs that can run on supported async backends; create_task_group() scopes sibling tasks. async with anyio.create_task_group() as tg: tg.start_soon(worker, item) is the common AnyIO task-group pattern. AnyIO task-group APIs differ from asyncio.TaskGroup method names, so mixing start_soon and create_task by memory is an easy mistake.
